questions.question: What did Meg like to build with boxes before she went to Maker School?
questions.explanation: Helps children recall Meg's passion and curiosity, connecting her interests to the idea that everyone can be creative in their own way.

questions.question: How did Meg feel when Simone made box creations too? Why do you think she felt that way?
questions.explanation: Encourages children to recognize and talk about feelings when meeting someone similar or when feeling challenged, which can help build empathy and understand social situations.

questions.question: What happened when Meg and Simone argued and didn't want to work together during the Maker Match?
questions.explanation: Shows the direct outcome of not working together and helps children see why cooperation is important.

questions.question: Why do you think the big box creation fell down? What could Meg and Simone have done differently?
questions.explanation: Encourages kids to think about consequences of actions and to problem-solve ways to do better through teamwork.

questions.question: What did Meg and Simone do to fix their project after it broke? How did working together help them?
questions.explanation: Highlights the positive results of teamwork, reinforcing the story's moral in a concrete way.

questions.question: Have you ever worked on something with a friend or family member? How did it feel to work together?
questions.explanation: Connects the moral lesson to real-life situations so children can relate and share times they've worked together with others.

questions.question: What are some things you could build or make with friends if you shared ideas, like Meg and Simone did?
questions.explanation: Promotes creative thinking and shows children how sharing ideas can lead to more fun and exciting projects.

questions.question: How did Meg and Simone feel at the end of the story? Why do you think they became friends?
questions.explanation: Helps children understand the reward of cooperation—friendship—and makes a clear connection between positive behavior and positive outcomes.

questions.question: If you and a friend want to make different things, what could you do to work together like Meg and Simone did?
questions.explanation: Encourages practical thinking about solving disagreements and finding ways to combine ideas, reinforcing the moral of teamwork and sharing.

moral: When we work together and share ideas, we can create amazing things and make new friends.
learning_objectives: Children will recognize the value of working together and sharing ideas.
Children will identify feelings that come from working alone versus working as a team.
Children will learn how to connect the story's lesson to their own experiences at home or school.
Children will practice thinking of ways to solve disagreements in a kind, cooperative manner.
